content: When caring for patients with suspected or confirmed Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) or Marburg Virus Disease (MVD), healthcare workers should wear two pairs of gloves if maintaining a distance of at least one meter from the patient is not possible. Research is needed to evaluate the effectiveness of various personal protective equipment (PPE) options, both individually and as a complete ensemble, through simulation studies. Additionally, PPE designs should accommodate the anatomical and hygiene needs of both men and women, including considerations for menstrual hygiene for female healthcare workers. The recommended PPE for contact with patients with suspected or confirmed EVD or MVD includes the following: Scrubs Closed-toe shoes Two pairs of nitrile gloves A medical mask combined with eye protection (either a face shield or goggles) A coverall Head and neck covering (with eye protection worn underneath) A disposable or reusable apron Contact refers to activities involving direct or indirect interaction with the patient or their environment. Reusable goggles or face shields must undergo proper decontamination procedures. Training on PPE use, ensuring continuous availability of PPE, and protocols for reuse or disposal are essential for effective implementation. Eye protection, such as goggles or face shields, should provide a good seal with the skin, be fogand scratch-resistant, and fit securely without becoming loose during clinical activities. Face shields, made of clear plastic, should provide full coverage of the face and sides, be fog-resistant, and fit snugly against the forehead. Both options are acceptable, but face shields are often preferred due to better visibility, comfort, and reduced fogging. Medical or surgical masks should be fluid-resistant, provide good breathability, and have a structured design to prevent collapse against the mouth. Masks should always be worn with appropriate eye protection. During aerosol-generating procedures, particulate respirators (e.g., N95) are recommended for added protection. Masks should be changed when wet, and wearing multiple masks simultaneously is not advised. The use of two pairs of gloves is generally recommended, as it provides additional protection. Gloves should fit well, be of high quality, and be available in multiple sizes to accommodate different hand sizes. Nitrile gloves are preferred due to their durability and resistance to punctures. Head and neck coverings are necessary when using gowns instead of coveralls, especially in high-risk settings or when there is a risk of splashes or sprays. Coveralls that include head and neck coverings eliminate the need for additional coverings. Disposable aprons should be single-use only and changed between patients whenever possible. Reusable aprons must be properly decontaminated before reuse. Healthcare workers should be trained on PPE use, including risk assessment to determine appropriate PPE based on patient symptoms and contact level. Masks and eye protection should be used together to provide comprehensive protection. Research is needed to compare the effectiveness of different PPE options and to address gaps in knowledge about the transmission of filoviruses, including the potential for airborne transmission. Proper training, availability of high-quality PPE, and adherence to infection prevention protocols are critical for effective implementation.
